messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Any student interested in giving a Stan talk for the Center for Cognitive Science at Rutgers?
parts:
Hi all. I got the following request; see below. Are there any students on this list who feel comfortable giving a talk on Stan for this cognitive science group? It could be a fun opportunity for the right student. If you’re interested just drop me an email.
A

On Sep 24, 2014, at 4:20 PM, Brian McMahan <bc...@cs.rutgers.edu> wrote:

> Hi Andrew,
>
> My name is Brian McMahan and I am a PhD candidate affiliated with the Rutgers University Center for Cognitive Science (RuCCS).
>
> We have a couple of talk series at RuCCS that revolve around many different topics in perception and cognition. I proposed inviting one of your students to talk about STAN at our Monday talk series and the organizer (Eileen Kowler) liked the idea. I was wondering if you had any recommendations of students who would/could come down to Rutgers to give a talk (about an hour trip down the NJ Transit NE Corridor line; travel cost reimbursed, of course).
>
> Thank you for your time!
> Brian McMahan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Any student interested in giving a Stan talk for the Center for Cognitive Science at Rutgers?
parts:
I really like the interdisciplinary nature of RuCCS and
had a great time the last time I was there for a workshop
on language processing (psych, philosophy, comp sci).

If you're interested (or otherwise need to give a presentation
that includes something about Stan), I have a recent set of
slides in PDF form with LaTeX source sitting on this branch on
GitHub:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/feature/issue-705-overview-talk

It's in directory src/docs/talks/paris-dauphine-2014. Feel free to
re-purpose as you see fit if you need to give a talk about Stan.
We're releasing all of our doc under the very generous CC-BY license.

- Bob
